title: The move that left without you
situation: You are practising on a [[demo-account|demo account]]. EUR/USD has risen 60 pips in the last hour without you. Your plan says to buy only on a pullback to a level you marked this morning, and price is nowhere near it. You feel you are missing out.
question: What do you do next?

responses.text: Buy now at market before it goes any higher.
responses.explanation: This trade comes from the feeling, not from your plan. Chasing a move often means a worse entry and no clear place for your stop.

responses.text: Stay out, write the move in your journal, and keep waiting for your planned level.
responses.explanation: Your plan did its job: it kept you out of a trade it did not cover. Noting the move lets you review it calmly later.

responses.text: Buy a small size now, just to be in the trade.
responses.explanation: Smaller size limits the damage, but it is still a trade outside your plan. It also trains the habit of acting on the urge.

responses.text: Place a [[pending-order|pending order]] at the level your plan marked, with your usual [[stop-loss|stop loss]].
responses.explanation: This turns the plan into an order. If price comes back, you are in on your terms. If not, you missed nothing your plan wanted.

takeaway: A move you missed is not a loss. The next trade only counts if it fits your plan.
